In /bench/repo (Go project, memos fork), answer with exact path:line citations:

(1) Default installation (no database flags): which database driver is the default? Check cmd/ flag defaults (search for "sqlite" default in cmd/memos or cmd/main.go and profile package internal/profile or server profile). Then find the concrete method that executes the SQL INSERT when a memo is created: store/db/<default driver>/memo.go CreateMemo. Cite the factory that selects the driver (store/db/db.go NewDBDriver) with path:line, the default value definition path:line, and the concrete CreateMemo path:line.

(2) Markdown processing behind an interface: search internal/markdown for an interface type (e.g. Service/Parser/Renderer interface), the concrete implementation(s), who constructs them (constructor call sites in server startup or elsewhere), and which components hold/store the interface value (struct fields of type that interface). Cite path:line for interface decl, impl decl, construction site(s), holder struct fields.

(3) Memo derived metadata: each memo has a payload/property computed from its content (tags, has_link, has_task_list, etc.) used for lists/previews. Find where it's computed (e.g. a memoproperty/memopayload package or function like RebuildMemoPayload), which operations trigger recomputation (CreateMemo handler, UpdateMemo handler, any background runner), and what properties it extracts. Cite path:line for the computation function, each trigger call site, and the extracted fields.

Return concise findings.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
Findings.

## (1) Default DB driver: sqlite

- Default flag/config value: `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go:122` (`viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")`) and `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go:130` (`rootCmd.PersistentFlags().String("driver", "sqlite", ...)`).
- Profile field + sqlite-specific DSN defaulting: `/bench/repo/internal/profile/profile.go:30` (`Driver string`), `/bench/repo/internal/profile/profile.go:110` (`if p.Driver == "sqlite" && p.DSN == ""` → `<data>/memos_prod.db`).
- Driver factory: `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:14` (`NewDBDriver`), sqlite branch at `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:19-20`.
- Store wrapper: `/bench/repo/store/memo.go:109` `(*Store).CreateMemo` → `s.driver.CreateMemo`.
- Concrete INSERT: `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16` `func (d *DB) CreateMemo`; the statement is built at `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go:41` (``INSERT INTO `memo` (...) VALUES (...) RETURNING ...``).

## (2) Markdown behind an interface

- Interface decl: `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:31` `type Service interface` (methods: ExtractAll, ExtractTags, ExtractProperties, RenderMarkdown, RenderHTML, GenerateSnippet, ValidateContent, RenameTag).
- Concrete impl: `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:58` `type service struct { md goldmark.Markdown }` (goldmark-backed; methods from line 108 onward).
- Constructor: `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:84` `func NewService(opts ...Option) Service`; options `WithTagExtension` (`:68`), `WithMentionExtension` (`:76`).
- Construction sites: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48` (inside `NewAPIV1Service`, with both tag + mention extensions), and test helper `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44`. Production entry is `/bench/repo/server/server.go:76` (`apiv1.NewAPIV1Service`).
- Holder struct fields of type `markdown.Service`:
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35` `APIV1Service.MarkdownService`
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:45` `RSSService.MarkdownService` (injected from the API service instance at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:85`; ctor `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:58`)
  - `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16` `Runner.MarkdownService` (ctor `:19`)
- Other consumers: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32` (ExtractAll for mentions), `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:85` (GenerateSnippet), `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:339` (RenderHTML).

## (3) Memo derived payload

- Computation entry point: `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74` `RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, markdownService)` — calls `ExtractAll` at `:80`, assigns `memo.Payload.Tags` (`:85`) and `memo.Payload.Property` (`:86`).
- Actual extraction logic: `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:352` `(*service).ExtractAll` (single AST walk); equivalent standalone property pass at `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:184` `ExtractProperties`.
- Extracted fields (proto `MemoPayload_Property`, `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto:15-22`, generated `/bench/repo/proto/gen/store/memo.pb.go:85-93`): `has_link`, `has_task_list`, `has_code`, `has_incomplete_tasks`, `title` (first H1). Plus `tags` (`memo.proto:12`) and mentions (returned in `ExtractedData`, `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:21-25`, but only tags/property are persisted into payload).
- Trigger call sites:
  - Create: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` (in `CreateMemo`, before `s.Store.CreateMemo` at `:115`).
  - Update: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447` (only inside the `path == "content"` branch of `UpdateMemo`'s update-mask loop; sets `update.Payload`).
  - Batch/background: `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27` `(*Runner).RunOnce` rebuilds all memos in batches of 100 — note this runner is **never constructed in production code**; `grep` shows no `memopayload.NewRunner(...)` call site (`/bench/repo/server/server.go:162` only wires `s3presign.NewRunner`), so payload recomputation happens only on the two API paths above.
- Consumption: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:48-49` (tags + property into the API `Memo`), converter at `:315`; user stats aggregate tags at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:138` and `:254`.

Gap worth flagging: `markdown.Service.RenameTag` (`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:410`) has no production caller, so no tag-rename path exists that would need payload rebuilds.
